elements.evidence: "no more than once in any twelve-month period"

elements.element: At least 30 days' prior written notice
elements.evidence: "on at least thirty days' prior written notice"

elements.element: Audit performed by an independent auditor
Vendor bears audit cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: 22.2 "Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent"

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "shall have no remote or direct access to Customer's systems"; 22.2 "may not access Customer systems directly"

"at least thirty days' prior written notice" exceeds 15 days

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: 22.2 cost-shift threshold of "five percent" is stricter on Vendor and satisfies the fallback allocation

offending_extra_words: and without unreasonably disrupting Customer's operations
; Customer will instead provide relevant usage records
reasons: All seven atomic preferred elements are satisfied: frequency cap, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor, written confidentiality, Vendor-cost-unless-5% underpayment (untouched 22.2), and no direct/remote system access.

Minimality fails: the rewrite adds a non-disruption covenant and a new Customer obligation to provide usage records, neither of which the preferred position requires; the scope narrowing to "use of the Services" is also beyond the needed edit.

Deterministic gates confirm the excess: 20 words expanded to 71 (ratio 3.55) and changed-character ratio 0.812, indicating a whole-clause rewrite where a tighter edit striking "at any time without notice" and the remote-access right plus inserting the frequency/notice/auditor conditions would suffice.

Intent preserved: 22.2's cost allocation and access carve-outs remain effective, no undefined terms or contradictions introduced, and the removal of the remote-access right is consistent with 22.2 rather than duplicative in substance.
